original_question: Does there exist a maximal curve X over a finite field F_{q^2} whose Frobenius dimension is 3, whose Frobenius linear series has second generic D-order epsilon_2 = 2, and which has an F_{q^2}-rational point P with second (D,P)-order j_2(P) = 3?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting case (B) in the paper’s introduction: the existence problem asking whether there exists an F_{q^2}-maximal curve with Frobenius dimension 3 such that the second generic D-order is ε_2 = 2 and there is an F_{q^2}-rational point P with second (D,P)-order j_2(P)=3. The paper answers this affirmatively, first by an explicit example in Theorem 4.1 and then by an infinite family in Theorem 5.4.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact mathematical configuration the paper isolates as one of its three open existence cases: an F_{q^2}-maximal curve, Frobenius dimension 3, second generic D-order ε_2=2, and an F_{q^2}-rational point P with j_2(P)=3. It also uses the paper’s notation ε_2 and j_2(P) in the intended sense.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient object is not just any curve over F_{q^2}, but an F_{q^2}-maximal curve, i.e. a projective, geometrically irreducible, nonsingular algebraic curve over F_{q^2} with #X(F_{q^2}) = q^2 + 1 + 2gq.
The Frobenius linear series should be named explicitly as D = |(q+1)P_0|, where P_0 is any F_{q^2}-rational point of X.
The phrase “Frobenius dimension is 3” means dim(D)=3.
The symbol ε_2 should be identified as the second generic order of the Frobenius linear series D, i.e. in the generic D-order sequence (0,1,ε_2,q).
The symbol j_2(P) should be identified as the second order in the (D,P)-order sequence at the point P.
The quantifier in the paper is existential in q as well: the question is whether such a case occurs for some prime power q, not for every q.
The point P should be stated explicitly as P ∈ X(F_{q^2}).
To stay paper-faithful, the question should be framed as whether case (B) actually occurs among maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3, matching the introduction’s formulation.
refined_question: Does there exist, for some prime power q, an F_{q^2}-maximal curve X of Frobenius dimension 3—that is, with Frobenius linear series D := |(q+1)P_0| for an F_{q^2}-rational point P_0 and dim(D)=3—such that the generic D-order sequence is (0,1,ε_2,q) with ε_2 = 2, and such that there exists a point P ∈ X(F_{q^2}) whose (D,P)-order sequence has second entry j_2(P)=3?
justification: The introduction states that, after recalling the restrictions on ε_2 and on the possible values of j_2(P) for maximal curves with Frobenius dimension 3, Cossidente–Korchmáros–Torres asked whether three specific cases occur. Your draft matches case (B) exactly, except that the paper formulates it in the language of the Frobenius linear series D on an F_{q^2}-maximal curve and treats “Frobenius dimension 3” as dim(D)=3. The paper then says Theorem 4.1 gives an affirmative answer to (B), and Section 5/Theorem 5.4 strengthens this by constructing an infinite family of such maximal curves. So the sharpest paper-faithful stand-alone question is the existence of case (B), with D and the order notation explicitly defined.

citations.label: Introduction, case (B) in the list of three existence questions
